newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM Hun Sen blasts human rights groups.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM Hun Sen blasts human rights groups.

text.p: Co-Premier Hun Sen on Tuesday lashed out at human rights workers in Cambodia, accusing them of elitism and urging donor countries to suspend funding for their activities.

"Other countries should reconsider their funding to human rights organisations in Cambodia, whose workers wear ties and sit in meetings, saying 'human rights, human rights'," Hun Sen told a local U.N. Human Rights Day ceremony.
The co-premier, who was speaking at a school in this town 10 km (six miles) south of the capital, did not say whether he was referring to local or international groups.

There are a handful of international human rights organisations based in Cambodia, including the U.N. Centre for Human Rights, and about 30 local groups involved in human rights activities, rights workers said.

"Some human rights organisations only sit in a room with air conditioning and take information from the real human rights organisations in the field, taking the opportunity to shout, 'human rights, human rights' in order to collect high salaries from donor countries," he said.
The second prime minister vowed to celebrate future Human Rights Days in the provinces and not Phnom Penh. Hun Sen had declined to participate in a Phnom Penh ceremony this year.
His comments followed the release last week of a Human Rights Watch/Asia report, which said that Cambodia was winding up its worst year for human rights since U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
The report, titled "Cambodia: Deterioration of Human Rights," said political violence, torture, killings and interference with press freedom had all increased in 1996.
